title: The Missing Sudo Grant
description: Add a colleague to the sudo group and produce a written audit of what they may run.
scenario: Jordan from the on-call rotation was promised sudo access on this staging box, but every elevated command he runs fails with 'permission denied'. On Debian/Ubuntu systems sudo is granted by membership of the sudo group — and he is not in it. Fix the membership, then write down exactly what he is now allowed to run so the change is auditable.
symptoms: jordan's sudo commands fail even though he knows his password
`groups jordan` does not list the sudo group
The operations handbook requires a written record of every sudo grant
No audit file exists for this change yet
mission: Add jordan to the sudo group, then save `groups jordan` and the `sudo -l -U jordan` privilege listing into /home/intern/sudo-audit.txt.

hints.title: The sudo group
hints.content: On Ubuntu, membership of the sudo group is what allows a user to escalate. Check it with `groups jordan`.

hints.title: Grant it
hints.content: `sudo usermod -aG sudo jordan` — the same -aG pattern as any other group.

hints.title: Ask sudo itself
hints.content: `sudo -l -U jordan` shows exactly which commands the user may run — ideal evidence for an audit record. You can run it because your intern account has passwordless sudo in this lab.

acceptance_criteria.description: jordan is a member of the sudo group
audit file records the sudo privilege listing
